fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Front Entry Area; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of approach on the street.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders can identify it quickly without searching along the street frontage.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris to allow full-width passage at all times.
• Create a designated turnaround area near the detached structure or open lawn to allow fire apparatus and emergency vehicles to reverse direction without backing long distances.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain clearance wide enough for emergency vehicles to pass without stopping.
• Cut back tree branches overhanging the access drive to a height that allows ladder trucks and tall emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Thin dense vegetation between the road and the main residence so responders can see the structure and front entry from the driveway approach.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure to create a clear working space around the exterior walls.
• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing accessible without a key or code, or provide responders with the combination through your local fire department's knox box or equivalent program.
• Post the gate access method with your local fire department so responders are not delayed waiting for entry.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Grass Cover; Limited Vegetation Separation; Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Long Driveway; Woody Debris; Mixed Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all trees and shrubs that are touching or directly next to the house on all sides.
• Thin the tree clusters nearest to the house to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove dead branches, fallen limbs, and woody debris from the ground around the house and outbuildings.
• Cut or mow grass around the house and keep it short, especially during dry months.
• Scatter or remove piled woody debris visible near the structures.
• Separate shrubs from one another where they grow close together near the house so fire cannot move easily between them.
• Trim overhanging tree branches along the full length of the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Remove low-hanging branches from trees near the house up to at least 10 feet from the ground.
• Clear grass, shrubs, and dead plant material from both edges of the driveway for its full length.
• Thin the scattered trees between the house and the outer tree clusters to break up the continuous vegetation leading toward the structure.
• Remove any shrubs or tall grass growing immediately against the foundation or walls of the house.
• Keep the area around any outbuildings or detached structures clear of loose plant material, shrubs, and woody debris.
